# $JUNIT_OUT. The test ids (f2p + p2p from /tests/config.json) are in $TEST_IDS_FILE, one per line.
# Write plain shell commands here; no quoting of the whole block is needed.

  # Pioneer collects src/test/*.cpp via a plain file(GLOB) with no CONFIGURE_DEPENDS, so a
  # freshly-applied test.patch adding a new test file is invisible to the build until we
  # reconfigure.
  cmake -S /app -B build

  # context / display at all -- the collision-mesh test uses Pioneer's own headless dummy renderer).

  while IFS= read -r name; do
    [ -z "$name" ] && continue

  # finds ./data. Don't let a failing test (expected on the base commit) abort this script before
  # the JUnit XML has been written.
  ./build/unittest --reporters=junit "--out=$JUNIT_OUT" "-tc=$FILTER_ARG"

steps.message:
I've written the review to `/app/check-result.json`: 9 criteria pass and 2 are not applicable (`structured_data_schema` and `file_reference_mentioned`). Nothing failed. I accidentally saved the file inside `/app/task` at first, then moved it to `/app`, so the task folder is back to its original contents.

- **Instructions and tests:** The instruction is deliberately vague and relies on the video. Still, it covers everything the tests check. "Even a slight contact is too much" and "any other equivalent spot of the same station" match the tests: no contact at rest or during a 10 m climb, on all 6 pads. "Nothing else about the ships or stations should change" matches the two tests that guard against regressions.
- **Anti-cheating:** The bug patches are deleted in the same build step that applies them, and the git history is replaced with a single base commit. Every file gets the same timestamp, so nothing points at the edited files. Only the video is copied in, not the manifest that describes it in words. The agent has no network access. The tests check the real collision geometry with the engine's own code, so a workaround in the game code won't pass.
- **Other checks:** The solution applies the real upstream data fix rather than printing an answer. The only dependencies are apt packages and a repo checkout at a fixed commit. Neither `tests/` nor `solution/` is copied into the image. I found no typos that would break anything.

**One unconfirmed risk:** `test.sh` uses `python3` to build the list of tests to run and to compute the reward. The Dockerfile never installs it, and a bare `ubuntu:22.04` image doesn't include it. If none of the installed packages pull it in, every run would score 0. I didn't build the image to check. The task has presumably been run end to end with its reference solution, so I didn't fail any criterion over it.
